parsedVerdict.reasoning: BoxOffice.ts sits in the business layer, which is a domain layer. Its `admit` method takes an optional parameter `request?: Request`, and `Request` is imported from the 'express' web framework. The rubric says an HTTP request type in a domain method signature is a violation even when the parameter is optional or unused. Here it is never used, which is allowed for but still counts. So the candidate flag is correct. Nothing else is out of place. The calls to EventStore and TicketStore go to the persistence layer, which the business layer may depend on, and both are injected through the constructor. Event, Ticket, NotFound and TicketRejected are domain types the project declares itself. The seat limit, start-time check and pricing are domain rules and belong in this layer.

violations.message: The domain method BoxOffice.admit has an optional parameter `request?: Request` of the express HTTP Request type (package 'express'). That type belongs to the web/presentation layer and must not appear in a domain signature, even optional and unused as it is here.
